task.description:
Resolve ISS-0207. `HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` section 1.2 (created yesterday-in-run-time by WF03-ISS0204-20260821, commit ef62d4b) quotes a corpus measurement as reproducible and states exact bucket counts. Two of those buckets -- total files scanned, and the gap-zero count -- grow with every handoff the pipeline writes, so the figures are stale by construction. The gate on that very run re-ran the command three minutes later and got 607/469 against the asserted 606/468. It reconciled exactly (to that run's own step-03b handoff), so nothing was wrong -- but the section gives a later reader no way to tell expected growth from a defect. The finding is stated first-hand by the REVIEWER that raised it, in `handoffs/WF03-ISS0204-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json` `result.issues` (third entry); `docs/issues/ISS-0207.yaml` carries ORCH's filing of the same.

THIS IS A FRAMING FIX, NOT A REMOVAL, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE TASK. Section 1.2's argument rests on that measurement; a fix that weakened it into vagueness would cost more than the staleness does. Do not delete a figure, do not soften the command into a description of a command, and do not replace counts with words like 'most' or 'the majority'. What changes is the framing around the numbers, so that a re-run reconciles rather than alarms.

WHAT TO DO, IN ORDER:

1. RE-RUN the section 1.2 measurement command yourself first, verbatim, from the repo root. You need a current reading to write an accurate as-of marker, and you need to know first-hand which buckets moved since ef62d4b and by how much. Note that the corpus has grown again since the gate's 607 -- this run's own handoff files are in it. Report your numbers.

2. DETERMINE the commit the original figures were measured at, from git rather than from prose. The measurement was taken during WF03-ISS0204-20260821's Step 03; `git log --oneline` and `git show --stat` over `docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` will identify the commit that introduced section 1.2. State how you determined it.

3. EDIT section 1.2 so that all four acceptance criteria hold. Concretely, the section must end up saying: the date and the commit the figures were measured at; which buckets grow with the corpus and which are stable (a bucket like the 25 negative-gap files is a fixed historical set that only grows if the defect recurs -- which makes it an ALARM if it moves, the opposite of the file count, and that asymmetry is worth stating because it is what makes the marker useful rather than merely defensive); and that the finding the measurement supports is the SHAPE -- the roughly 5:1 ORCH-stamped-to-agent-stamped ratio, and the negative-gap class concentrated on round `:00` minutes -- not the absolute counts.

4. KEEP THE ONE-CANONICAL-STATEMENT PROPERTY that ISS-0204 established. Section 1.2 is the single statement of this rule; section 1 step 3, section 3's table row and `ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 6 are pointers. Your edit stays inside section 1.2 and must not push any part of the rule out into another file, and must not add a second as-of marker anywhere else.

5. CLOSE the issue (WF-03 Step 5, taken within this step): `docs/issues/ISS-0207.yaml` gets `status: resolved`, `resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0207-20260821`, `resolved_at:` from a real clock read. Close GH#398 with `gh issue close 398 --comment "..."` naming this run and the issue file.

6. COMMIT `docs/` and your own handoff file. Do NOT write `handoffs/registry.json` or `handoffs/orchestrator.log` -- both are ORCH's.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Docs-only run. Do not touch `lib/`, `priv/repo/migrations/`, `test/` or `web/`.
- Do not touch `docs/issues/ISS-0206.yaml` or anything it describes. ISS-0206 is a separate open issue against the same section 1.2, covering two unrelated wording gaps, and it will be worked as its own run. Leave its subject matter alone even though you are editing the same section -- fixing it here would take a later run's work without its gate.
- Do not retroactively edit historical handoff files, and do not correct the 25 negative-gap or 10 null-`started_at` files. They are the evidence.
- Timestamps come from the clock at the moment you write each one. Read the clock in its OWN command, then write -- never batch `date -u` and the write that consumes it into one shell command; see the new first entry in `docs/anti-patterns.md`, which ORCH added after doing exactly that twice during the previous run's closure.
- Your handoff's `started_at` was stamped by ORCH at dispatch, per section 1.2's own rule. Do not touch it. Claim by setting `status` to `IN_PROGRESS` only.
acceptance_criteria: Section 1.2's quoted figures carry a dated as-of marker naming both the date and the commit they were measured at, with the commit identified from git rather than from prose
The text states which buckets grow with the corpus and which are a fixed historical set, and that growth in the former is expected and reconcilable rather than a discrepancy
The finding the measurement supports is stated as the shape -- the ratio and the negative-gap class -- rather than as the absolute counts
No figure is deleted and the command remains quoted verbatim and reproducible; the diff is additive framing, not a weakening of the evidence
The measurement was re-run first-hand and your own current numbers are reported with the drift reconciled against ef62d4b's figures
The edit stays inside HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.2; no part of the rule or the marker is copied into ORCHESTRATOR.md or core-directives.md
docs/issues/ISS-0207.yaml carries status: resolved, resolved_in_run and a clock-read resolved_at; GH#398 is closed
ISS-0206's subject matter is untouched, and no file outside docs/ and handoffs/WF03-ISS0207-20260821/ is modified

result.summary: ISS-0207 resolved. All six numbered steps executed in order; all eight acceptance criteria met. (1) MEASUREMENT RE-RUN FIRST-HAND, verbatim, from the repo root, before any edit -- the fenced python heredoc in S1.2 exactly as printed. My numbers: 608 files, 0 unparseable, 10 null started_at, 470 gap==0, 14 gap 1-30s, 89 gap>30s, 25 negative, 20 of those with created_at on a round :00 minute. Against ef62d4b's asserted 606/0/10/468/14/89/25/20 the drift is +2 files and +2 at gap zero and NOTHING ELSE. It reconciles to the unit and I enumerated the cause rather than assuming it: a second pass over the corpus printing every handoff with created_at >= 2026-08-21T10:18:05Z (the moment ef62d4b's author measured) returns exactly two files, WF03-ISS0204-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json (created_at == started_at == 10:20:01Z, gap 0) and this run's own WF03-ISS0207-20260821/step-03-date-scope-figures.json (created_at == started_at == 10:31:11Z, gap 0). Two new files, both at gap zero: +2/+2, which is the observed drift and no residue. This also chains cleanly through the ISS-0204 gate's intermediate reading of 607/469 at 10:23:10Z -- that gate saw the first of the two, I see both. Every fixed bucket (10 null, 14, 89, 25 negative, 20 round-minute) is unmoved, which is the positive evidence that no negative-gap file has recurred and the historical corpus has not been edited. (2) COMMIT IDENTIFIED FROM GIT, NOT PROSE. `git log --oneline -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` lists ef62d4b 'docs(ISS-0204): settle started_at' as the most recent commit touching the file; `git show ef62d4b -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` grepped for added lines confirms its diff is the one that ADDS both the '## 1.2' heading and the '606 files, 0 unparseable' figures paragraph. Full sha ef62d4b13427d752aed4553eee1cbf9a479ddea0, committed 2026-08-21 15:17:44 +0500 (= 10:17:44Z). Being the newest commit on the file also establishes that no later commit altered the figures, so the marker's date and commit are the correct pair. (3) EDIT: THREE NEW PARAGRAPHS INSERTED INTO S1.2, immediately after the figures paragraph and before 'What the discriminator CANNOT distinguish'. Para 1 is the as-of marker -- 'AS OF 2026-08-21, at commit `ef62d4b` -- and a later re-run will NOT reproduce every figure, by design' -- naming the full sha, stating it was identified from git log over the file, telling the reader to re-run and RECONCILE rather than read a mismatch as a defect, naming `files` and `gap==0` as the two buckets that grow (one file per handoff written, landing at gap zero under this very rule), giving the reconciliation procedure (the difference must equal the handoffs written since ef62d4b, enumerable by created_at), and working both re-runs to date: 607/469 at the gate (+1/+1) and 608/470 here (+2/+2). Para 2 states the asymmetry: the 25 negative-gap, the 20 round-minute, the 10 nulls, and now also the 14 and 89 (since agent-stamping is forbidden outright) are a CLOSED historical set that nothing written under this rule can join -- so more than 608/470 is routine growth, while any movement in 10/14/89/25/20 is an ALARM meaning either the negative-gap class recurred or the corpus was edited, with 'do not silently update the figure; find out which'. Para 3 states that the finding is the SHAPE -- the ~5:1 ORCH-stamped-to-agent-stamped majority and the negative-gap class concentrated on round :00 minutes -- not the absolute counts, both surviving any corpus growth. (4) FRAMING, NOT REMOVAL, AND ONE-CANONICAL-STATEMENT PRESERVED. `git diff --numstat` on HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md: 32 insertions, 0 DELETIONS -- purely additive, mechanically proving no figure was deleted, the python heredoc untouched and still verbatim, and no count softened into 'most' or 'the majority'. The edit is confined to S1.2 between the figures paragraph and the CANNOT-distinguish paragraph; ORCHESTRATOR.md, core-directives.md, S1 step 3 and S3's table row were not opened for edit and are unchanged in the commit (`git show --stat dd31ad6` lists only HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and ISS-0207.yaml). No second as-of marker exists anywhere. (5) ISSUE CLOSED. docs/issues/ISS-0207.yaml: status: resolved, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0207-20260821, resolved_at: 2026-08-21T10:34:43Z from `date -u` read in its own command immediately before the write, plus a `resolution:` block recording the measurement and what changed. GH#398 closed via `gh issue close 398 --comment` naming this run and the issue file; gh confirmed 'Closed issue tvolodi/letflow#398'. (6) SCOPE. Docs-only: nothing under lib/, priv/repo/migrations/, test/ or web/ touched. ISS-0206's subject matter -- the missing threshold for 'immediately' in S1.2 step 2, and the unclosed null-started_at loop between S1 step 3 and S1.2's last paragraph -- is deliberately untouched; my para 2 references the existing no-backfill paragraph as a cross-reference only and does not state or resolve what ORCH should do about a reported null. No historical handoff file was edited and the 25 negative-gap and 10 null files were left uncorrected -- confirmed by my own re-run still finding them at 25 and 10. handoffs/registry.json and handoffs/orchestrator.log were not read-modified or staged by me and remain uncommitted for ORCH; `git diff --numstat` shows 20/0 and 6/0, insertions only, zero deletions on both. TIMESTAMP DISCIPLINE: both clock reads (resolved_at, completed_at) were taken by a `date -u` command of its own, with the write that consumed each issued as a separate later call, per the new first entry in docs/anti-patterns.md. This handoff's started_at (10:31:11Z, ORCH's dispatch stamp) was not touched; the claim was status -> IN_PROGRESS only, and completed_at 10:35:58Z follows it.
result.next_action: ORCH: verify the two docs files against this artifacts_out list, then decide whether this run needs a REVIEWER gate (ISS-0204's own settlement got one; this is a smaller, purely additive framing edit on the same section). Record this handoff's commit sha in git_evidence if you want it captured, then close the run: push dd31ad6 plus the handoff commit, release queue task 207, and commit registry.json and orchestrator.log -- both are yours, both are still uncommitted in the tree, and both are append-only clean (20/0 and 6/0). ISS-0206 remains open against the same section and is the natural next run; its subject matter was left untouched here.
